entities.label: Institution
entities.summary: San Carlo al Lazzaretto is a small Renaissance style octagonal church now in largo Bellintani Fra Paolo, number 1 in Milan, Lombardy, Italy. It is located about three blocks northwest of the gate known as Porta Venezia, which gave name to the quartiere. Its present situation, amidst crowded 19th and 20th century apartment blocks, has little relationship to its original placement, inside the central park of a massive rectangular cloister-like 15th-century leprosarium (Lazaretto). The church, once called Tempietto di Santa Maria della Sanità or San Carlino, escaped the late-nineteenth century demolition of the Lazzaretto.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: San Carlo al Lazzaretto's preservation amidst urban development highlights the importance of historical architecture and the resilience of religious institutions in the face of modernization. Its original placement within a leprosarium underscores the complex history of healthcare and quarantine practices in medieval Europe.
